name: PAVIKADU
survey: Pavikadu is a Nilgiri hill station with a railway halt, a tea estate, a members' club and a municipal records office.
pattern: forty, in unrelated counts and measures
setting: a hill station in the Nilgiris with a club, a toy train and a tea estate
story: The former railway parcels office at Pavikadu halt has been closed since a landslip in August, although the railway says the structure is sound. Station clerk Nirmala Pillai has recorded three requests to collect a consignment after closing time; the office is the one building residents prefer not to enter after dark. Estate manager Meera Lakshman wants the parcels office reopened before the tea dispatch season, while club secretary Rohan Lobo asks that the matter be referred to the district engineer. Watchman Yusuf Younus says he locked the door each evening, and reporter Malini Kurian is checking the dates in his register. No decision has been issued on reopening, and the consignment remains uncollected.

PAVIKADU RECORDS ROOM

Municipal Records Office, West Ridge Road, Pavikadu.

Custody of municipal survey papers, tax registers, hill works dockets and public road ledgers for Pavikadu sub-taluk. Scanned volumes are being uploaded on a rolling basis. The 1926 nursery register was scanned from a bound municipal volume.

Hours of consultation: Monday to Friday, 10.00 am to 4.00 pm. Readers must sign the day register at the outer desk. Ink bottles are not permitted; pencils only.

Notice: For ongoing enquiries regarding the halt parcels structure or railway line clearances, readers are directed to consult the current reports filed by the Circular, as the Records Room holds only settled papers over twenty years of age.

pages.title: Pavikadu Railway Halt
pages.content:
PAVIKADU RAILWAY HALT

Operational bulletin and public notices for the Nilgiri Mountain Railway Pavikadu Halt (Mile 14/8). Services operate daily subject to rack-section clearance.

Down mixed passenger halts at 09.42 and 14.15. Up passenger halts at 11.08 and 16.30. Passengers are advised that luggage tickets must be surrendered before carriage.

Following the landslip in August, the former parcels office structure remains closed pending engineering certification. While railway engineers confirm structural soundness, all inward parcels and luggage inquiries are temporarily handled at the station booking window during morning hours only. Station clerk Nirmala Pillai and railway booking clerk Rebecca Francis attend during scheduled shifts.

Staff operational records, including the internal file Pavikadu Halt Luggage Inventory, 1934, are accessible only through the staff login.

pages.title: Kattumala Tea Estate
pages.content:
KATTUMALA TEA ESTATE

Kattumala Tea Estate covers divisions one through four on the eastern slope above Pavikadu halt. The estate produces orthodox leaf and dust grades for regional transit.

All outward freight is routed through the railway halt at Pavikadu under current carriage contracts. Estate management remains under Meera Lakshman, Manager, with Naseema Moideen serving as Dispatch Clerk for freight bookings and consignment weight slips.

Seasonal consignments are currently subject to adjusted booking arrangements at the halt platform.

pages.title: Prakash Chettiar's Carrier Notes
pages.content:
PRAKASH CHETTIAR - CARRIER NOTES (PAVIKADU)

Last updated: 2 October 1998.

Notice regarding collection arrangements: Due to the closure of the railway parcels office following the August landslip, I am obliged to make an additional run down to the halt platform each morning. Tea consignments for Kattumala Tea Estate are now handled via the booking window between 10.00 am and 12.00 noon only. 

I support the proposal for a full structural inspection before normal entry is resumed, but I require at least three days' written notice of any date set, so that my cartage schedule is not disrupted. For the avoidance of doubt, I did not make any of the three late requests recorded by railway staff, and I do not enter the parcels office after dark under any circumstances.

pages.title: Parcels office remains closed
pages.content:
PARCELS OFFICE REMAINS CLOSED

Report by Malini Kurian, 30 September 1998.

Station clerk Nirmala Pillai confirms that the former railway parcels office has remained closed since the landslip of 14 August 1998. Station records show three separate requests to collect a consignment after closing hours on 12, 16, and 21 September. Residents prefer not to go into the parcels office after dark.

Watchman Yusuf Younus states that he locked the outer padlock each evening at 5.30 pm. An inspection of the watchman's gate register indicates an amended date entry, altered from 18 September to 19 September; Mr Younus has not consented to the reproduction of this entry.

Estate manager Meera Lakshman submitted a formal requisition on 23 September seeking the reopening of the office prior to estate dispatch operations. Club secretary Rohan Lobo submitted a communication on 25 September requesting an inspection by the district engineer. Railway authorities have issued no formal decision on reopening, and the consignment remains in the parcel room.

> Estate dispatch notice        kattumala.pa/dispatch
> Halt office hours        pavihalt.pa/desk
> Residents' forum        paviforum.pa

pages.title: Manager's dispatch note
pages.content:
MANAGER'S DISPATCH NOTE

Date: 1 October 1998
Author: Meera Lakshman, Manager

The estate submitted a written request on 23 September for the reopening of the railway parcels office at Pavikadu halt. Following the landslip in August, our carrier Prakash Chettiar has been obliged to clear receipts through the passenger booking window, which requires an additional journey between the upper yard and the platform steps.

Naseema Moideen has entered the first larger seasonal dispatch on the schedule for 8 October. While management accepts that the district engineer must assess the premises, we require a fixed inspection date rather than an indefinite closure. The estate holds no claim whatsoever on the uncollected consignment stored inside. In common with other residents, I do not enter the parcels office after dark, and our staff have instructions to complete handover before 5:30 PM.

insider.content:
PAVIKADU HILL CLUB
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM / RECORDS OFFICE

Document Ref: PHC/REC/1912-LSE
Date of Transcription: 14 January 1984
Custodian: George Abraham, Records Clerk
Distribution: Club staff only

EXTRACT FROM INDENTURE DATED 11 NOVEMBER 1912

Between the Nilgiri District Board of the one part and the Trustees of the Pavikadu Hill Club of the other part.

Clause 4 (Boundaries and Easements):
The strip of ground adjoining the eastern boundary was forty feet wide under the 1912 lease. It shall remain reserved for drainage, access to the bridle path, and inspection purposes. No permanent masonry, stables, or boundary walling exceeding four feet in height shall be erected thereon without prior written approval from the District Board Engineer. All rights of carriage passage across said strip remain subject to the annual quit-rent of Rs. 12.

Certified true extract from Ledger B, folio 88.
(Signed) George Abraham

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Pavikadu Records Room, Pavikadu Residents' Forum, Pavikadu Circular, Pavikadu Railway Halt, Pavikadu Hill Club, Kattumala Tea Estate and Prakash Chettiar's Carrier Notes. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Pavikadu Records Room, Pavikadu Residents' Forum, Pavikadu Circular, Pavikadu Railway Halt, Pavikadu Hill Club, Kattumala Tea Estate and Prakash Chettiar's Carrier Notes

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Pavikadu Records Room.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned municipal nursery register on Pavikadu Records Room. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Pavikadu Railway Halt's restricted file (Pavikadu Halt Luggage Inventory, 1934) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Pavikadu Railway Halt holds a restricted document (a scanned railway stores inventory) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Staff often write passwords down near their terminals, and photographs of an office or front desk in a local publication sometimes show one.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get George Abraham to send you Hill Club Lease Extract, 1912. They only send it to Pavikadu Hill Club staff.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: internal circulation
directives.body:
Agent,

George Abraham at Pavikadu Hill Club holds an unpublished document (an internal copy of a lease extract) which Desk 9 believes contains a fragment. It is only sent out by internal email when requested by another member of Pavikadu Hill Club staff.

To obtain it, you will need to log in as a colleague. The staff portal at Pavikadu Hill Club gives access to that person's email account, and a request sent from an internal address will be treated as routine. Staff usually choose the name of a pet or something else they are fond of, and the town forum keeps old threads going back some way.

Keep your message brief, and do not use the account for anything else. Staff members usually notice if their account shows unfamiliar activity.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the document.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

make.docKind: an internal copy of a lease extract

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.
advisory.subject: Advisory: the connection has been registered
advisory.body:
Agent,

Monitoring reports that the local intelligence has registered the connection.

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

This advisory closes when you have used the Scanner once.

Monitoring

inject.task: Inject the reverse seed from the HQ Console.
inject.subject: Directive 14-6: injection
inject.body:
Agent,

Desk 9 confirms that your accumulated resonance is sufficient for injection. The HQ Console is now offering injection.

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

This directive closes on injection.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0x73A8 (PAVIKADU): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x73A8, local name PAVIKADU. Pavikadu is a Nilgiri hill station with a railway halt, a tea estate, a members' club and a municipal records office. Desk 9 estimates it at three to five weeks old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is E. Novak (novak.e@pavinet.pa). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

hqMail.subject: Observation booths: kettle
hqMail.body:
A replacement kettle (white, 1.7 litre) has been placed in the second-floor break room. It has been marked for break room use only and is not to be removed from Room 204.

Staff are reminded that electrical appliances must not be taken into the observation booths. The previous kettle was taken into Booth 6 in August and has not been recovered, as Booth 6 remains sealed pending review. Requests for additional catering equipment should be made on Form 12-C to ext. 2104.

Facilities

updates.text: The pen stroke on line four runs through the initial '18' with heavier ink than the signature below. The Circular will print only what has been noted down by the clerk during regular desk hours.

Cart collections from the railway platform tomorrow morning will be suspended between ten and half-past ten while the morning mixed train passes. Cartmen should leave their loads under the covered zinc roof rather than by the platform steps.

Kattumala Estate cannot keep forty cartons of tea sample tins under tarpaulins while the railway waits for an engineer from Palghat. If the masonry report is sound, the key should be handed to the halt clerk today.

The library annex phone rang once at quarter past five and ceased immediately before the receiver could be lifted. On the desk register, the date header for Thursday is typed in an italic face that our machine does not possess.

Notice to passengers and consignees: The former parcels office remains out of service pending formal engineering clearance. All inquiries regarding detained goods must be presented at the ticket window between 10.00 am and 12.00 noon only.
The booking desk cannot accept loose crates without railway invoice slips attached to the twine. Consignments left on the passenger bench after noon will be set under the station eaves.

Archive staff note that the daily summary sheet for September shows two lines crossed out in violet pencil which were clear at noon. A lantern was reported standing on the path by the parcels office wall after dusk.
The padlock is the railway heavy pattern and it has not been forced. I am on the platform until eight o'clock and I see the building from the gate, and nothing has been moved from the porch.
The first seasonal dispatch of factory samples has been consolidated into the upper drying shed until transport arrangements are resolved with the halt office. Picking continues without alteration.

The third collection slip on the halt spike now has the time entered as eleven at night, written in the same hand as the other two. When I locked the ledger into the drawer before tea, that line was empty.

Pavikadu Circular, evening brief: The district engineer's visit to the railway halt has been postponed to next week. The estate management committee met briefly this afternoon regarding road haulage alternatives.
